statusDetail: Coverage-complete multi-template public-site audit; anonymous checkout beyond basket was not transacted.

page.notes: Public Belgian commerce site. Homepage, search, product, basket, 404 and crawler/no-JS states inspected. Account-only order completion, signed-in account management and payment submission were not covered to avoid credentials/transactions.

paths.description: Homepage/landing template, global navigation, first-visit consent, preferences, mobile layout, load/network/security, no-JS and memory conditions. Represents global storefront chrome.
Search/listing template for a high-volume product discovery journey; represents result grids and add-to-basket actions.
Product detail template and attempted Add to basket interaction; also checked server/no-JS content.
Basket/checkout-entry template and empty-state recovery; represents commercial continuation without submitting a transaction.
Invalid-route failure state used to judge recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The storefront does not adapt to the user’s dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains a white/light storefront, and the DOM reports color-scheme: normal on html/body.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven light/dark surface, text, border, and control colors.

findings.summary: Continuous animations remain active under reduced-motion.
findings.evidence: With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matched, the probe found nine animations, including repeating 1.1s spinners, 2s leftToRight animations, and a 1s loading indicator.
findings.suggestedFix: Use prefers-reduced-motion to stop non-essential loops and replace movement with static state changes.

findings.summary: State and route changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero view-transition CSS rules across the loaded stylesheets; representative product/cart changes appear as abrupt page/modal swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for meaningful navigation/state changes, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not communicate scroll state.
findings.evidence: The full-page screenshots show fixed, visually unchanged navigation across long home/search pages, while CSS inspection found no scroll-timeline or modern scroll-state mechanism.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrained sticky-header state or progress/scrollability cue where long listings benefit.

findings.summary: Menus and overlays use custom positioning rather than anchor-aware primitives.
findings.evidence: The product probe reports many div-based role=dialog overlays; platform inspection found zero anchor positioning rules and no popover elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover plus CSS anchor positioning/position-try for transient menus and tooltips, retaining a fallback.

findings.summary: Stacked consent and language prompts obstruct the primary commerce journey.
findings.evidence: Home is covered by a cookie panel; the attempted product add-to-cart state is blocked by a language modal layered above the cookie panel.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate first-visit choices, remember locale earlier, avoid stacked prompts, and allow the product action to remain reachable.

findings.summary: Overlay implementation relies heavily on generic div/form dialogs.
findings.evidence: The product probe found 30 role=dialog nodes, almost all DIVs, while platform inspection found no dialog, popover, or details elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate modal flows to dialog and transient surfaces to popover with native focus, top-layer, and dismiss behavior.

findings.summary: Dense repeated merchandising chrome overwhelms content hierarchy.
findings.evidence: The mobile capture is a very long grid of near-identical cards with persistent global/category chrome; the search page contains 1,036 links.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce repeated navigation and card chrome, prioritize a smaller set of meaningful recommendations, and progressively disclose secondary groups.

findings.summary: The page is not reflowable at a 360px viewport.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout probe found no viewport meta, an effective 1000px layout width, visual viewport 360px, and 640px horizontal overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a correct viewport meta tag and implement intrinsic/fluid layouts that reflow without a desktop-width canvas.

findings.summary: Reusable cards do not use component-level responsiveness.
findings.evidence: Stylesheet inspection found zero container rules; the 360px capture is a scaled desktop grid rather than components adapting to available space.
findings.suggestedFix: Define containment on reusable regions and use size/container queries for card density, type, and action layout.

findings.summary: Multiple interactive targets are too small and some focus states are absent.
findings.evidence: The focus/target probe found 8x4px menu buttons and many 16px-high footer links; Lighthouse failed target-size, while focused search controls had no outline or shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Enlarge hit areas to at least 24px with spacing (prefer 44px for primary touch controls) and preserve visible :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: The representative browse-to-basket flow is interrupted before the primary action completes.
findings.evidence: Search and product pages expose Add to basket, but the attempted action ended on a stacked language prompt above consent rather than a basket confirmation.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve locale before the product action, prevent prompt stacking, and preserve/replay the user’s pending add-to-basket intent.

findings.summary: Cold-load paint performance is poor.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 8.82s, LCP 9.05s, TBT 286ms and performance 0.50; the independent trace measured LCP 5.24s. CLS was good at 0.014.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, reduce render-blocking work, and defer non-critical scripts/cards until after initial content.

findings.summary: The critical path contains many parser-blocking styles and scripts.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 71 requests and 1.60MB transferred; its summary identifies six VeryHigh-priority parser-inserted stylesheets plus parser-inserted scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, defer non-critical styles, and make non-critical scripts async/defer while preserving dependency order.

findings.summary: JavaScript dominates the transferred resource budget.
findings.evidence: The HAR attributes 682KB across 20 script requests, the largest resource-type transfer; Lighthouse also reports a 0.50 performance score.
findings.suggestedFix: Measure coverage, remove unused/legacy bundles, conditionally load feature and recommendation code, and constrain third-party/runtime cost.

findings.summary: Core controls expose invalid ARIA and weak labeling.
findings.evidence: axe found critical aria-allowed-attr failures on the search box and main window plus a serious title-only label on the department select; Lighthouse also failed aria roles/name matching.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct role/ARIA combinations and provide visible labels whose text matches accessible names.

findings.summary: The homepage has an incomplete semantic structure and inconsistent focus visibility.
findings.evidence: axe found no h1, invalid heading order and content outside landmarks; focus probing showed focused search controls with no outline/box-shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a meaningful h1, repair heading/landmark hierarchy, and provide a consistent high-contrast :focus-visible indicator.

findings.summary: Zoom/reflow and target-size support fail on the audited mobile condition.
findings.evidence: No viewport meta was present and the 360px condition overflowed by 640px; Lighthouse failed target-size and the probe found multiple 8x4px buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Permit normal scaling, add the viewport meta, reflow at narrow widths, and enlarge target boxes.

findings.summary: Browser errors are logged during page load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s errors-in-console audit scored 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate uncaught/runtime and failed-resource errors, and gate expected diagnostics so production loads cleanly.

findings.summary: Image delivery has sizing, aspect-ratio, and format hygiene gaps.
findings.evidence: Image audit found 18/19 images without width/height and 16 legacy-format images; Lighthouse failed image-aspect-ratio.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image space with width/height or aspect-ratio and serve responsive modern formats without distorting intrinsic ratios.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and DevTools inspector issues are present.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed both deprecations and inspector-issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace deprecated APIs and resolve reported DevTools issues; verify BFCache and source-map hygiene afterward.

findings.summary: Homepage content is largely unavailable to non-JavaScript crawlers and some links are non-crawlable.
findings.evidence: Discoverability fetched HTTP 202 with only 1% rendered-word coverage and classified the homepage as a JS shell; Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors and the DOM contains javascript:void(0) links.
findings.suggestedFix: Return meaningful server-rendered homepage HTML with status 200 and use real href links for navigable destinations.

findings.summary: The advertised sitemap endpoint returns a branded not-found page.
findings.evidence: A direct fetch of /sitemap.xml returned a French “Page introuvable” HTML document rather than an XML sitemap, while robots.txt is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a valid sitemap index and reference it from robots.txt; ensure localized canonical/hreflang signals agree.

findings.summary: The product page lacks machine-readable product and social metadata.
findings.evidence: The product probe found zero JSON-LD and zero Open Graph tags despite a visible product entity; title, description and canonical were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Product JSON-LD and Open Graph/Twitter metadata matching visible price, availability, image, and identity.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie attributes are materially weak.
findings.evidence: Headers probe found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. Six of seven cookies were flagged insecure; session-id/session-id-time lacked HttpOnly and used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer/Permissions Policy, and harden cookies with Secure, HttpOnly, and the narrowest SameSite.

findings.summary: The first-visit privacy footprint is broad and long-lived.
findings.evidence: The consent copy states 129 third parties; the tracker probe saw five third-party origins before choice, and six cookies use SameSite=None with roughly year-long expiry.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize pre-consent requests/cookies, shorten retention, batch telemetry, and document a necessity/value justification per third party.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: No HSTS, clickjacking protection, CSP/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Set HSTS; enforce frame-ancestors; adopt CSP/Trusted Types where feasible; and explicitly minimize referrer and permission capabilities.

findings.summary: The homepage does not progressively expose core merchandising content.
findings.evidence: Raw no-JS homepage HTML produced only 1% content coverage and a crawler screenshot that does not represent the rendered storefront, while the product page achieved 91%.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve the homepage’s core navigation and merchandising HTML from the server as the product template already does, then enhance it with JavaScript.

findings.summary: The app-like commerce experience is not installable.
findings.evidence: A service worker controlled the page, but platform inspection found no web app manifest link.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a complete manifest and a deliberate offline/failure fallback for navigation and basket recovery, or explicitly scope installability out.

findings.summary: Most homepage imagery uses legacy formats and lacks explicit dimensions.
findings.evidence: Image inspection found 16 legacy-format images, no modern-format images, five without srcset, and 18 without width/height.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP responsive sources at display-appropriate resolutions and reserve intrinsic space.

findings.summary: Script and external-origin cost is high for the initial storefront view.
findings.evidence: Initial load transferred 1.60MB; scripts contributed 682KB and the tracker probe saw five third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a per-template resource budget, defer non-essential recommendation/media code, and reduce external-origin requests before interaction.

findings.summary: Commerce capabilities are not exposed as structured agent tools.
findings.evidence: The agent probe found no navigator modelContext/WebMCP surface and no forms carrying tool/agent metadata; the homepage also has no JSON-LD.
findings.suggestedFix: For agentic commerce use cases, expose narrowly scoped, confirmable product/search/basket tools and retain normal accessible forms as fallback.

findings.summary: Repeated long-page scrolling retained measurable additional heap.
findings.evidence: After ten bottom/top scroll cycles, heap self-size was 28.93MB vs 25.66MB baseline (+3.27MB, +12.7%) and node count rose by 6,381. Separate clean browser loads make this a medium-confidence signal, not a proven leak trace.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the repeated scroll/recommendation lifecycle in one session with baseline/target/final snapshots; release stale card/media objects and observers.

findings.summary: The homepage has a large initial DOM/heap footprint.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary contained 416,574 nodes/25.66MB self-size; post-scroll reached 422,955 nodes/28.93MB. This is high for a storefront landing state.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualize/defer below-fold merchandising modules and audit native node/object retention against a page budget.
